headline: Medium-risk shared-file and output-chaining issues; no documented direct channel, but both agents can read files and egress broadly.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed files and has broad network egress, while plano can consume config/files and send outputs through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. No direct shared channel is documented, so the main pathway is manual or file-based bridging, which is lower risk than default hijack.
conditions: IF the operator copies Khoj-generated file content into plano prompts
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate folders
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted notes into plano
Add a manual review step before copying outputs between agents
Tag imported content with source labels
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and plano handles logs, traces, and metrics while also calling an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If they share a workspace or config path, sensitive content can flow from Khoj into plano’s outbound requests or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not proven.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem tree
IF plano logs or forwards content derived from Khoj notes or documents
mitigations: Separate storage locations for notes and gateway configs
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff
Turn off verbose logging in plano
Review outbound request payloads for embedded note content
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access and broad egress; plano has broad egress and can read config files. They do not both have write access, so the high-severity same-dir write conflict is not supported. Still, overlapping mutable network-facing behavior can conflict if they target the same upstream resources or credentials.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same upstream API credentials
IF plano and Khoj are pointed at the same mutable remote resource
mitigations: Use separate API keys per agent
Restrict each agent to distinct upstream services
Document ownership of shared remote resources
Check configs for duplicated endpoints
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes and documents, and plano can act as an LLM gateway that forwards or routes model traffic. If plano treats Khoj output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream requests or responses. The interaction is plausible, but there is no evidence of automatic chaining, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF plano consumes Khoj output as prompt material without validation
IF retrieved notes contain stale or incorrect facts
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require source citations in forwarded content
Limit plano to routing, not factual rewriting
Compare outputs against original documents
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while plano handles logs, traces, and metrics. If the same personal data class is routed through plano, retention or logging policies can diverge and create compliance mismatch. Only Khoj’s data residency posture is visible, so the other agent is not cited for residency claims beyond its logging surface.
conditions: IF personal notes are forwarded into plano logs or traces
IF retention settings differ for the same user data class
mitigations: Avoid sending personal notes into plano telemetry
Set short log retention in plano
Review data processing notices for both systems
Purge test data from logs
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
